# Fireactions — GitHub Actions runners on Firecracker microVMs

A runner **is** a microVM: fireactions schedules a pool of them and hands each job a fresh one.
Everything that makes a microVM work applies (see the `firecracker` skill), plus the pool's own
constraint.

## The constraint that decides whether a pool can run at all

Fireactions configures containerd with a snapshotter chosen in the layer's `containerd:` connection, and
the accepted set is **exactly two**: `devmapper` and `blockfile` — the fork's `SnapshotterBacksRootDrive`
accepts nothing else, because `native` and `overlayfs` cannot back a microVM root drive. `devmapper`
needs a **spare block device**, so on a host with none — a plain workstation — the pool cannot start,
and the failure names containerd rather than the missing device. The snapshotter is therefore the field
to look at FIRST when a pool will not come up.

The device-less path is `blockfile`, and it takes two layers to work: `opencharly/layer-containerd`
**serves** it — the plugin CLONES a pre-existing scratch image, so the layer creates and formats that
file before the daemon starts, and without it the plugin reports `error` rather than `ok` — and
`opencharly/layer-fireactions` declares `snapshotter: blockfile` in its `containerd:` connection. Its bed
then asserts the **daemon-reported** served set, which is the check that cannot pass by accident:
a grep of the rendered config would pass while the substrate could not start.

## The fork, and why it is pinned

The opencharly fork carries the changes this integration needs; consumers pin the **tag**, not a
branch. `v2.0.8-oc1` is the pinned release. Advance it only through the producer-first order:
fork PR → merge → tag → consumer pin bump.

## The pieces

- **the host layer** installs the VMM binary, the jailer and the fireactions kernel on the venue — the
  things a pool needs before any runner can exist;
- **the runner** is the pool member: a microVM booted from the root-drive + kernel pair;
- **the beds** are `check-fireactions-host` (the host layer lands and the pool's prerequisites are
  present) and `check-fireactions-runner` (a runner comes up on that host).

## Two traps worth knowing before you debug

- **A guest that needs plugins does not have them.** A deploy provides its target the host's charly
  binary and **nothing else** — no candy corpus — so any step that dispatches a plugin verb in the
  guest fails with an unknown word, and the fix is charly-side (opencharly/charly#916), not a
  workaround in the bed.
- **A candy referenced by a remote `@github` ref does not apply its `service:` block the way a local
  ref does** (opencharly/charly#918), which is why a layer that starts a unit can look installed and
  still have the unit inactive.
